title: Understanding MSE and MAE
text: Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) are two different metrics used to evaluate the accuracy of a model. MSE is sensitive to outliers because it squares the errors, while MAE is more robust to outliers as it takes the absolute value of errors.

title: Constant Model and Optimization
text: A constant model predicts the same value for all inputs. When optimizing a constant model, the choice between MSE and MAE can lead to different optimal predictions.

title: Median vs Mean in Optimization
text: When optimizing for MAE, the optimal constant prediction is the median of the data. For MSE, the optimal constant prediction is the mean of the data.

title: Comparing Training Loss
text: Consider a dataset with outliers. Which metric, MSE or MAE, would result in a lower training loss when using the median as the constant prediction?

title: Effect of Outliers on MSE and MAE
text: If a dataset has significant outliers, which metric, MSE or MAE, is more likely to be affected by these outliers?
